summary.oneLiner: Revenue growth was driven by Europe and ARV despite Revlimid phase-out, while EBITDA margin held at 20.4% ex-Revlimid; key catalysts include Pen-G ramp-up, biosimilar launches in Q3-Q4, and Lannett integration, all supporting margin expansion and cash flow strength.
summary.business: Aurobindo develops, manufactures and commercialises high-quality, affordable medicines worldwide, spanning generic formulations, specialty products and active pharmaceutical ingredients across regulated and growth markets. Its finished-dosage portfolio covers oral solids, liquids, injectables, OTC, derma and biosimilars across CNS, cardiovascular, antibiotics, ARV, anti-diabetics, gastroenterology, oncology and dermatology, sold to generic customers, major pharma customers, institutional customers and healthcare professionals. The API business supports both captive requirements (53% of APIs captively consumed) and external customers including innovators and large generic companies, and the group is building future-ready platforms in biosimilars and biologics contract manufacturing.

Formulations: Generic and branded specialty finished dosage products across oral solids, liquids and injectables
Adquey (difamilast) ointment 1% - topical treatment of mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis (Acrotech, USFDA approved)
MDI/DPI products, transdermals and derma foams (specialty generics pipeline)
Biosimilars / Biologics: CuraTeQ biosimilars portfolio (two biosimilars approved by EMA, one approved by Health Canada during FY26)
Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients & Inte: Beta-lactams including sterile and non-sterile Penicillin, Cephalosporins and Penems

currentContext.expansion: Aurobindo operates 32 modern manufacturing and packaging facilities across several countries (28 in India and one each in the USA, China, Portugal and Brazil) plus 6 R&D centres spread across 16,000 sq.m, and states it is continuously expanding led by backward integration into key starting materials (KSMs) and intermediates. Backward integration across Pen-G, 6-APA and Amoxicillin is described as strengthening supply security, reducing import dependency and improving the long-term margin profile; the Pen-G facility was successfully commercialised and stabilised during FY26, and based on current operating levels management expects annualised Pen-G production to exceed 10,000 metric tonnes with capacity utilisation levels exceeding 80% at consistent yields. In biologics, the Company launched TheraNym, its biologics CMO platform; commissioning activities for TheraNym Unit 1, a 60 kL integrated mammalian cell culture facility, are progressing as planned and are expected to be fully completed by the end of 2026, and the Company is separately expanding both bulk drug substance manufacturing and fill-finish capacities to support future growth and long-term manufacturing-readiness. In China, the OSD facility - which currently has a manufacturing capacity of 2 billion dosages - continues to scale up on the back of increasing product approvals and growing supplies into international markets, particularly Europe. The stated way-forward actions are to progress commercialisation and scale-up of the Dayton and Raleigh (USA) facilities with incremental capacities across oral, respiratory and transdermal product segments; to complete GMP certification for the Vizag facility and further strengthen it through the addition of cartridge filling lines, prefilled syringes (PFS) and BFS infrastructure; and to continue evaluating debottlenecking and brownfield expansion opportunities to enhance manufacturing flexibility, optimise asset utilisation and support long-term growth. Multiple capacity enhancement initiatives were advanced across manufacturing facilities during FY26 to support rising global demand. Geographic expansion is being pursued through new subsidiaries in Malaysia and the Philippines and entry into Algeria, Morocco, Egypt, Francophone West Africa, Ghana and Nigeria, adding to an operating footprint that already includes subsidiaries in South Africa, the UAE, Thailand and Saudi Arabia and greenfield operations in Tanzania and Kenya. Inorganic expansion comprises the ongoing Lannett acquisition in the US (to be completed and integrated subject to necessary regulatory approvals) and recent India acquisitions, while in Europe the Company remains focused on evaluating selective inorganic opportunities and expansion into new geographies. Analytical method transfers to Ace Laboratories in the UK de-bottlenecked testing at the Malta facility. The Chairman's/MD's strategic-priority KPI panel states 'Capex investments ~ ` 3,000+ crore' for FY26; this figure is presented as a KPI bullet and not as a labelled capex disclosure, so it is recorded here in narrative only and is not carried into capex_disclosed.

risks.risk: Regulatory compliance and product stewardship across multiple global regulators
risks.note: BRSR flags non-compliance with applicable regulatory requirements such as the US FDA, EMA, MHRA and WHO, and strict US/EU product-packaging rules, as risks that 'can lead to expensive product recalls and reputational damage'. The manufacturing review records that seven units received EIRs from the US FDA during the year, and consumer/customer complaints numbered 4,056 filed in FY26 with 752 pending resolution at year-end (4,593 filed and 641 pending in FY25) - so inspection outcomes and complaint volumes are a live watch-item for a company whose entire turnover is regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing.

risks.risk: Geographic and channel concentration in the US and Europe, with US revenue exposed to transient product sales
risks.note: The US and Europe together accounted for 73% of total revenue in FY26. The US formulations business was down 3% y-o-y, 'primarily impacted by lower transient product sales' - a reminder that a material part of US revenue is opportunistic rather than base business. Industry commentary in the same section notes intensifying loss-of-exclusivity dynamics (impact expected to rise to USD 179 billion from USD 49 billion in the prior five years) and increasing scrutiny over drug pricing and reimbursement policies in the US.

risks.risk: API pricing pressure, competitive intensity and geopolitical risk in emerging markets
risks.note: API segment revenue declined 6% y-o-y in FY26, with the Company stating business sales moderated 'due to pricing pressure in the antibiotics portfolio, intense competition and geopolitical risks in select emerging markets'. The outlook explicitly describes the API business as 'dynamic, shaped by pricing pressure, competitive intensity and geopolitical uncertainties'. Margin protection currently depends on the mix shift towards non-antibiotics.

risks.risk: Dependence on institutional ARV procurement, with PEPFAR funding expected to moderate
risks.note: The ARV business is anchored in institutional channels including PEPFAR, the Global Fund and the Government of South Africa. Management states 'PEPFAR support is expected to moderate gradually over the coming years', shifting the procurement landscape towards the Global Fund and local government funding, which 'could also increase the relevance of local manufacturing and packaging capabilities in select markets' - a structural change in how this segment's demand is sourced.

risks.risk: Antimicrobial resistance and antibiotic manufacturing effluent
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative financial implications: improper management of antibiotic waste during manufacturing can release APIs into the environment, contaminating aquatic ecosystems and fuelling AMR, and the Company concedes that 'effective and scalable solutions to manage this risk are still being sought'. Mitigation is membership of the AMR Industry Alliance. This is structurally material given the scale of the beta-lactam / antibiotics portfolio.

risks.risk: Climate transition and energy cost/regulation exposure
risks.note: BRSR identifies Climate Change as a Risk with negative implications: stricter climate regulations, renewable energy mandates and emissions reduction targets impose transition risk requiring higher compliance costs, operational changes and significant investment in low-carbon technology, while extreme weather events can disrupt supply chains, cause resource scarcity and inflate raw material costs. Energy Management is separately flagged for rising energy costs, stringent regulatory savings targets and the fossil-to-renewables transition.

risks.risk: Supply chain sustainability, human-rights compliance and new disclosure regimes
risks.note: Sustainable Supply Chain is flagged as both risk and opportunity: climate disruption raising raw material and logistics costs; legal penalties from instances of forced labour, child labour or excessive working hours in the chain; and stricter global regulation such as India's BRSR Core and the EU's CSDDD 'demanding extensive supply chain-related disclosures' that require significant investment in process set-up and reporting systems. Awareness training on the Supplier Code of Conduct has so far reached suppliers accounting for 77% of key starting material (API) suppliers.

risks.risk: Talent attraction/retention and occupational health & safety across a 40,000-strong workforce
risks.note: Workforce Wellbeing is flagged for a dynamic and highly competitive job market, with limited growth opportunities or skill mismatches leading to disengagement, increased attrition and productivity loss; the Company employed 27,000+ permanent and 13,000+ contractual employees as of March 31, 2026. Occupational Health and Safety is a separate Risk with negative implications - 'gaps in adherence to safety protocols, lack of real-time monitoring, or insufficient training risk recurring safety failures, leading to enforcement actions and reputational damage'.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Aurobindo develops, manufactures and commercialises high-quality, affordable medicines worldwide, spanning generic formulations, specialty products and active pharmaceutical ingredients across regulated and growth markets. Its finished-dosage portfolio covers oral solids, liquids, injectables, OTC, derma and biosimilars across CNS, cardiovascular, antibiotics, ARV, anti-diabetics, gastroenterology, oncology and dermatology, sold to generic customers, major pharma customers, institutional customers and healthcare professionals. The API business supports both captive requirements (53% of APIs captively consumed) and external customers including innovators and large generic companies, and the group is building future-ready platforms in biosimilars and biologics contract manufacturing.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global pharmaceutical industry grew 9.3% in 2025 to an estimated USD 1,939 billion from USD 1,774 billion in 2024, driven by rising chronic disease incidence, an ageing population, higher R&D investment, advances in biologics and biosimilars, personalised medicine and digital health.
- The global pharmaceutical market is estimated at USD 2.6 trillion by 2030, growing at a 5-8% CAGR (2026-2030), led by new products and patent expiries including the growing impact of biosimilars; usage is projected to reach 4 trillion defined daily doses by 2030.
- GLP-1 receptor agonist market estimated at USD 71 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 202 billion by 2033 at a 13% CAGR, driven by rising obesity/diabetes prevalence, new launches and combination therapies.
- Global oncology drugs market estimated at USD 242 billion in 2025, projected to grow from USD 267 billion in 2026 to USD 667 billion by 2034 at a 12% CAGR.
- Global immunology market of nearly USD 180 billion in 2024 growing at 4-7% CAGR to USD 234 billion by 2029, with growth moderated by biosimilar erosion as blockbuster brands lose exclusivity up to 2030.
- Loss-of-exclusivity wave is a direct opportunity: palbociclib, enzalutamide and olaparib all lose exclusivity in 2027, and PD-1 inhibitors pembrolizumab and nivolumab are expected to face biosimilar competition starting 2028.
- Global biologics CMO market estimated by industry at approximately USD 22 billion in 2025, growing to over USD 40 billion by 2030 at a 12-15% CAGR - the addressable market for TheraNym.
- Rising demand for antibacterials alongside the need to manage antimicrobial resistance, and growth in neurology/mental-health treatment markets, support the antibiotic and CNS portfolios.
- FY26 saw stable performance across businesses and markets supported by sustained demand, operational resilience and continued execution of strategic priorities; Europe crossed the EUR 1 billion revenue mark.
- Margin lever from the Taizhou facility commencing European supplies after receiving EU GMP and Chinese GMP, described as supporting margin improvement with a steady ramp-up in operations.
- Continued price erosion in certain ARV products, offset by efficient capacity utilisation, operational optimisation and award of new and supplementary contracts.
- Macro backdrop: global growth of 3.3% in 2025 expected to remain steady in 2026-27 with global inflation cooling to 3.8% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027; Indian GDP growth estimated at 7.7% in FY2025-26 with FY2026-27 real GDP projected between 6.8% and 7.2%; India-EU FTA concluded in Q4 FY2025-26 and an interim India-US bilateral trade deal signed.
- 888 cumulative ANDAs filed in the US as on March 31, 2026 with estimated total market potential of US$192 billion per IQVIA; 728 final approvals, 35 tentative approvals and 125 under review (160 ANDAs in different stages of review).
- During FY26 the Company filed 29 ANDAs with the US FDA including 4 for specialty products, and received final approvals for 37 products including 3 specialty products; 42 products launched in FY26.
- Eugia FY26: 54 global submissions across major markets (around 30 oncology-focused), 8 US ANDA filings, 31 approvals received and 38 launches across major markets.
- Eugia FY27 plan: 80+ global submissions planned and 30+ submission batches planned for regulated and semi-regulated markets; key planned submissions include Pen-G, Tirzepatide, Aztreonam, Cetrorelix, Lenacapavir and Avibactam + Ceftazidime; key planned launches include Nintedanib, Isosulphan Blue and Cyclosporine.
- First long-acting depot product, Paliperidone Palmitate, filed with the US FDA; four peptide products in advanced stages of development.
- Injectable specialty pipeline of 181 ANDA filings, including 144 approved products and 37 pending approvals; 195 injectable products in the portfolio including those under development.
- CuraTeQ pipeline of 14 biosimilar candidates at year-end, concentrated in oncology and immunology; approved/filed assets include Dazublys (trastuzumab), Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim), Zefylti (filgrastim) and Bevqolva (bevacizumab); BP16 (denosumab) and BP11 (omalizumab) completed Phase 3.
- Dermatology portfolio of 58 topical products and 12 transdermal patches including those under development; respiratory portfolio of 16 nasal spray products including those under development.
- Canada portfolio expanded to 220 approved products with 62 additional products awaiting final approval at the end of FY26; China had 18 product approvals up to March 31, 2026 with manufacturing planned across facilities in India.
- 1,100+ ARV dossiers filed globally (Company-wide).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Aurobindo operates 32 modern manufacturing and packaging facilities across several countries (28 in India and one each in the USA, China, Portugal and Brazil) plus 6 R&D centres spread across 16,000 sq.m, and states it is continuously expanding led by backward integration into key starting materials (KSMs) and intermediates. Backward integration across Pen-G, 6-APA and Amoxicillin is described as strengthening supply security, reducing import dependency and improving the long-term margin profile; the Pen-G facility was successfully commercialised and stabilised during FY26, and based on current operating levels management expects annualised Pen-G production to exceed 10,000 metric tonnes with capacity utilisation levels exceeding 80% at consistent yields. In biologics, the Company launched TheraNym, its biologics CMO platform; commissioning activities for TheraNym Unit 1, a 60 kL integrated mammalian cell culture facility, are progressing as planned and are expected to be fully completed by the end of 2026, and the Company is separately expanding both bulk drug substance manufacturing and fill-finish capacities to support future growth and long-term manufacturing-readiness. In China, the OSD facility - which currently has a manufacturing capacity of 2 billion dosages - continues to scale up on the back of increasing product approvals and growing supplies into international markets, particularly Europe. The stated way-forward actions are to progress commercialisation and scale-up of the Dayton and Raleigh (USA) facilities with incremental capacities across oral, respiratory and transdermal product segments; to complete GMP certification for the Vizag facility and further strengthen it through the addition of cartridge filling lines, prefilled syringes (PFS) and BFS infrastructure; and to continue evaluating debottlenecking and brownfield expansion opportunities to enhance manufacturing flexibility, optimise asset utilisation and support long-term growth. Multiple capacity enhancement initiatives were advanced across manufacturing facilities during FY26 to support rising global demand. Geographic expansion is being pursued through new subsidiaries in Malaysia and the Philippines and entry into Algeria, Morocco, Egypt, Francophone West Africa, Ghana and Nigeria, adding to an operating footprint that already includes subsidiaries in South Africa, the UAE, Thailand and Saudi Arabia and greenfield operations in Tanzania and Kenya. Inorganic expansion comprises the ongoing Lannett acquisition in the US (to be completed and integrated subject to necessary regulatory approvals) and recent India acquisitions, while in Europe the Company remains focused on evaluating selective inorganic opportunities and expansion into new geographies. Analytical method transfers to Ace Laboratories in the UK de-bottlenecked testing at the Malta facility. The Chairman's/MD's strategic-priority KPI panel states 'Capex investments ~ ` 3,000+ crore' for FY26; this figure is presented as a KPI bullet and not as a labelled capex disclosure, so it is recorded here in narrative only and is not carried into capex_disclosed.

- #1 generic pharma company in the US by prescriptions dispensed and extended units dispensed, with 10.8%+ share of all prescriptions dispensed in the US market (IQVIA TRX MAT March 2026 share of 10.5%)
- Top 4 market-share ranking across over 75% of the US product portfolio

- Europe in-house manufacturing contributes approximately 63% by value and 74% by volume, supporting cost competitiveness and supply assurance
- Broad European commercial footprint - 10 countries covering 85%+ of the European generics market, 1,600+ employees including a 500+ field force, leading positions in Portugal, France, the Netherlands and Spain
- Diversified channel presence across retail, hospital, OTC and tender channels
- Manufacturing breadth - 30+ manufacturing and packaging facilities worldwide, 6 R&D centres, 20+ facilities USFDA and EU GMP approved
- Leadership in the ARV market, particularly in Dolutegravir-based regimens which remain the standard of therapy; ranked No.1 among generic pharmaceutical companies in the 2026 Antimicrobial Resistance Benchmark by the Access to Medicine Foundation
- 90+ subsidiaries providing specialised capabilities and local market knowledge; 5 brands in South Africa hold No.1 position in their categories per IMS data
- Global workforce of 40,000+ and process-chemistry expertise supporting cost efficiency and affordability
